introduction: On this Sunday, the Book of Wisdom describes the wicked plotting against the righteous man. In the Gospel, Jesus again foretells his death, while his disciples argue about who is the greatest. He sets a little child among them and says that whoever wants to be first must be the servant of all. Saint James warns against jealousy and selfish ambition. Let us learn the greatness of humble service.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is the one who sustains our life. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that all who hold authority in her may serve, following the example of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For children, especially those who are unwanted, abused or neglected: that they may be welcomed and protected as Christ himself. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace in the world and in our homes: that we may overcome the jealousy and ambition that lead to conflict. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the righteous who are persecuted: that God may uphold them and deliver them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may seek not to be first, but to serve. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son came not to be served but to serve. Free us from jealousy and selfish ambition, and teach us to welcome the little ones in his name. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Servant of all
reflection.body:
The Book of Wisdom gives us a picture of how the wicked think about a good person who annoys them: "Let's test him with insult and torture, that we may find out how gentle he is." They mock his trust in God: if he is really God's son, let God save him. Christians have long heard in these words a description of the Passion of Jesus.

In the Gospel, Jesus tells his disciples for the second time that he will be handed over, killed, and rise on the third day. Mark notes sadly: "they didn't understand the saying, and were afraid to ask him." Instead, on the road, they argue about something else. When Jesus asks what they were discussing, "they were silent, for they had disputed with one another on the way about who was the greatest."

Jesus does not scold them. He sits down, calls the Twelve, and teaches them: "If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all." Then he takes a little child, holds the child in his arms, and says, "Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me." In that time, children had no status. To welcome them was to welcome someone who could give nothing in return.

Saint James explains where our conflicts come from: "For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed." He contrasts this with "the wisdom that is from above," which is "pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy."

We all have a little of the disciples' ambition. This week, look for a way to serve someone who cannot repay you: a child, an elderly person, someone overlooked. And when you are tempted to compete, choose instead to make room for someone else.
